## Problem statement

The proxy's `low` priority route (used by the priority-window cheap slot, 01:00–10:00 local, plus any explicit `X-Priority: low`) currently chains as `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` for the plan/author/code models. When the 2 local slots are saturated (a common overnight condition — see the 2026-10-19 proxy-usage-analysis report: fallback_after_queue 1657, munitoai-free rate limiting), low-priority traffic falls straight through to `munitoai-free`, which is capped at `rate_limit_rpm: 15` and returns HTTP 429s (16 upstream 429 events in the last window). Meanwhile the opencode-go provider entries sit idle and available during their off-peak UTC windows (`["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`, added by LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P) — precisely the hours when the cheap priority window is active and local is most contended.

Goal: allow low-priority work items to fall back to opencode-go when opencode-go is inside its off-peak `available_times` windows, so overflow local work during cheap hours is absorbed by an idle paid tier instead of being dropped on the rate-limited free tier.

## Context / constraints

- `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code is `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` (`proxy/config.yaml`). The `compact` model's low chain is `[opencode-go-compact, deepseek-flash-compact]` and is NOT in scope unless explicitly decided.
- The "low never spends on paid remote tiers" invariant (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA AC2 / priority.py `priority_routing_profile`) must be relaxed **only for off-peak-window-gated opencode-go entries** — the `available_times` gate (`provider.py _is_within_allowed_window`) keeps the paid spend confined to off-peak hours. Spending must remain blocked outside those windows.
- opencode-go entries in the plan/author/code model chains: `opencode-go` (OPENCODE_API_KEY), `opencode-go-2` (OPENCODE_2_API_KEY), `opencode-go-3` (OPENCODE_3_API_KEY) — all carry `available_times: ["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`.
- `available_times` are expressed in UTC; the cheap priority window is local time. Decide the intended alignment explicitly (and document it), since local vs UTC interpretation determines which hours opencode-go is actually reachable.

## Scope

Config + routing logic only. No llama-server changes. Evidence collection uses the proxy-usage-analysis skill (CLI: `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`) before and after.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Low-chain entry added:** the `low` priority_routes for plan, author and code include at least one opencode-go entry (after `munitoai-free`), with spend confined to the entry's off-peak `available_times` windows.
2. **Off-peak gating verified:** a unit test proves that when the opencode-go entry is outside its `available_times` window the low chain skips it (falls through to the next eligible provider), and inside the window it is tried — mirroring the existing timing-gate behaviour for other providers.
3. **Low-chain order preserved:** `local-qwen3` remains first when local has capacity; `munitoai-free` is attempted before paid opencode-go (free tier always preferred over paid when both are viable).
4. **Priority semantics intact:** medium/high chains are unchanged; the fully-paid `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` entries are NOT added to the low chain.
5. **No regression in retry-after / cooldown bookkeeping:** an off-peak opencode-go 5xx/429 does not poison the provider cooldown or stall circuit breaker for medium/high traffic (existing per-provider failure counters shared, not reset).
6. **Doc updated:** `proxy/config.yaml` `priority_routes.low` comments (and priority.py docstring if it states the paid-tier invariant) describe the off-peak opencode-go exception, including the UTC vs local window alignment decision.
7. **Tests + report:** full suite passes via `/skill:test`; run the proxy-usage-analysis report for a full window after the change and comment the work item with the before/after fallback-reason delta (`large_context_bypass`/`fallback_after_queue`/`context_too_large`/HTTP 429 counts), demonstrating that a share of low-priority overflow now lands on opencode-go during off-peak hours without increasing overall paid spend outside those windows.
data.title: Enable low-priority fallback to opencode-go during its off-peak windows

data.description:
# Reduce `munitoai-free` request budget to 2/minute

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want the `munitoai-free` provider entry to dispatch at
most **2** requests per rolling 60-second window (down from 15), so the free tier
is used sparingly and traffic spills to the paid tiers rather than burning the
quiet free allowance on bursts.

## Scope

- `proxy/config.yaml`: `rate_limit_rpm: 15` → `rate_limit_rpm: 2` on all three
  `munitoai-free` entries (plan / author / code).
- Docs that quote the shipped value: `proxy/docs/routing.md` (ships-with value +
  value history), `proxy/README.md` (reserve arithmetic `11 of 15`).
- No change to the gate, reserve, wait caps or any other provider.

## Notes

- With `rate_limit_rpm: 2` and `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3`,
  `floor(2 × 0.3) = 0` reserve slots, so new and in-progress sessions both see a
  cap of 2 per window (the reserve clamps to `rpm - 1`).
- Takes effect on the next proxy restart.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All three `munitoai-free` entries in `proxy/config.yaml` declare
   `rate_limit_rpm: 2`.
2. `proxy/docs/routing.md` and `proxy/README.md` state the shipped value of 2 and
   describe the resulting reserve/cap arithmetic correctly.
3. The changed-scope test gate passes (config-loading / fallback-chain tests).
4. Commit recorded on this work item and pushed to `dev`.
data.title: Reduce munitoai-free rate_limit_rpm to 2
